Title: Update order item status from MEASUREMENT_DONE to CUTTING_DONE and verify status is reflected in order details
Preconditions: An existing order with at least one item in MEASUREMENT_DONE status. User is logged in and has permission to update order statuses.
Steps:
1. Open the order details page for the existing order. Note the current status of the item (should show 'Measurement Done').
2. Navigate to the 'Update Status' section for the specific item.
3. Select 'Cutting Done' from the status dropdown.
4. Click 'Save' to update the status.
5. Refresh the order details page and verify the item status is updated.
6. Open the API response or detailed view (e.g., JSON response) for the order and locate the measurement group for this item.

Test Data: Order ID: 12345, Item: Formal Shirt, Initial Status: MEASUREMENT_DONE, New Status: CUTTING_DONE
Expected Result:
1. The order details page shows the item status as 'Cutting Done' after the update.
2. The API response or detailed view includes the measurement group for this item with the field 'orderItemStatus' set to 'CUTTING_DONE'.

Title: Verify order item status is displayed in order summary after creation
Preconditions: User is logged in and has permission to create orders. A customer and item are available for selection.
Steps:
1. Navigate to the 'Create New Order' page.
2. Enter customer details (e.g., name, phone, gender).
3. Select an item (e.g., 'Formal Shirt').
4. Add measurements for the item (e.g., Chest: 40, Waist: 34).
5. Mark the order as non-urgent and set a delivery date.
6. Click 'Save' to create the order.
7. Open the order details page for the newly created order.
8. Open the API response or detailed view (e.g., JSON response) for the order and locate the measurement group for this item.

Test Data: Customer: John Doe, Phone: 5551234567, Item: Formal Shirt, Measurements: Chest=40, Waist=34, Delivery Date: 7 days from today
Expected Result:
1. The order details page shows the item status as 'Measurement Done' by default.
2. The API response or detailed view includes the measurement group for this item with the field 'orderItemStatus' set to 'MEASUREMENT_DONE'.

Title: Verify that order item status is exposed in order responses only for authorized users
Section: Order Management - Order Item Status Exposure
Preconditions: 1. User is logged in with valid credentials. 2. User has at least one order with an order item in the system. 3. User has permission to view order details.
Steps:
1. Navigate to the 'My Orders' section in the application. 2. Select an order from the list to view its details. 3. Observe the order item details displayed on the screen, focusing on the status field.

Test Data: Use an existing order with an order item that has a status (e.g., 'MEASUREMENT_DONE', 'IN_PROGRESS').
Expected Result: The order item status (e.g., 'MEASUREMENT_DONE') is visible in the order item details for the authorized user.

Title: Verify that order item status is not exposed to unauthorized users in order responses
Section: Order Management - Order Item Status Exposure
Preconditions: 1. User is logged in with valid credentials but does not have permission to view order details. 2. An order with an order item exists in the system.
Steps:
1. Attempt to access the order details page directly via URL or API call (e.g., by guessing an order ID). 2. Observe the response or screen displayed.

Test Data: Use an order ID that the user does not have permission to access.
Expected Result: The application responds with an access denied message (e.g., 'You do not have permission to view this order') or a generic error page. No order item status or details are exposed.

Title: Verify that updating an order item status enforces proper authorization (insecure direct object reference) - unauthorized user cannot update another user's order item status
Section: Order Management - Order Item Status Update
Preconditions: 1. User is logged in with valid credentials but does not own the target order item. 2. An order item with a known ID exists in the system and belongs to another user.
Steps:
1. Navigate to the order item status update functionality (e.g., via API or UI form). 2. Enter the ID of an order item that does not belong to the logged-in user. 3. Attempt to update the status of the order item (e.g., from 'MEASUREMENT_DONE' to 'IN_PROGRESS'). 4. Observe the response or screen displayed.

Test Data: Use an order item ID that belongs to another user and a valid status transition (e.g., 'MEASUREMENT_DONE' to 'IN_PROGRESS').
Expected Result: The application responds with an access denied message (e.g., 'You do not have permission to update this order item') or a generic error. The order item status remains unchanged.

Title: Verify that updating an order item status rejects invalid status transitions
Section: Order Management - Order Item Status Update
Preconditions: 1. User is logged in with valid credentials and owns the target order item. 2. An order item with a known ID and status exists in the system (e.g., status is 'MEASUREMENT_DONE').
Steps:
1. Navigate to the order item status update functionality (e.g., via API or UI form). 2. Enter the ID of the order item. 3. Attempt to update the status to an invalid next step (e.g., from 'MEASUREMENT_DONE' to 'DELIVERED'). 4. Observe the response or screen displayed.

Test Data: Use an order item ID with status 'MEASUREMENT_DONE' and attempt to update to 'DELIVERED'.
Expected Result: The application responds with an error message indicating an invalid status transition (e.g., 'Invalid status transition from MEASUREMENT_DONE to DELIVERED'). The order item status remains unchanged.

Title: Verify that order item status is not leaked in error messages or logs during failed status updates
Section: Order Management - Order Item Status Exposure
Preconditions: 1. User is logged in with valid credentials. 2. An order item with a known ID exists in the system.
Steps:
1. Navigate to the order item status update functionality (e.g., via API or UI form). 2. Enter an invalid order item ID (e.g., 999999). 3. Attempt to update the status of the order item. 4. Observe the error message or log output displayed.

Test Data: Use an invalid order item ID (e.g., 999999) and a valid status (e.g., 'IN_PROGRESS').
Expected Result: The application responds with a generic error message (e.g., 'Order item not found') without exposing the invalid order item ID, current status, or internal system details (e.g., stack traces, database errors).

Title: Verify that order item status update enforces rate limiting to prevent abuse
Section: Order Management - Order Item Status Update
Preconditions: 1. User is logged in with valid credentials and owns the target order item. 2. An order item with a known ID exists in the system.
Steps:
1. Navigate to the order item status update functionality (e.g., via API or UI form). 2. Rapidly submit multiple status update requests (e.g., 10 requests in 1 second) for the same order item. 3. Observe the response or screen displayed after the first few requests.

Test Data: Use a valid order item ID and a valid status transition (e.g., 'MEASUREMENT_DONE' to 'IN_PROGRESS').
Expected Result: The application responds with a success message for the first few requests, then starts responding with a rate limit exceeded message (e.g., 'Too many requests. Please try again later.') for subsequent requests.
